newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Minister says new Malaysia airport delayed - Bernama.
newsitem.headline: Minister says new Malaysia airport delayed - Bernama.

text.p: Construction of Malaysia's new international airport in Sepang on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur is facing delays, Works Minister S. Samy Vellu was quoted by the national Bernama news agency as saying.
The main terminal complex, cargo complex and satellite buildings were all behind schedule, the minister said.

"Stern action should be taken against the contractors who failed to complete the packages on schedule to ensure the airport can be ready in September as planned," Bernama quoted the minister as saying.
Construction of the runway and the air traffic control tower had been completed on schedule, Bernama said.
The completion of the airport in time for the Commonwealth Games due to be held in Kuala Lumpur in 1998, is seen as vital for the smooth running of the event.
The airport is also one of the largest infrastructure projects in the country, costing around nine billion ringgit ($3.64 billion).

The construction of the 1.2-billion ringgit highway which links the airport to the new federal administrative centre Putrajaya, and information technology city "Cyberjaya", was progressing to his satisfaction, Vellu was quoted as saying.
